title: GS21 with a priced y chain and three exposure types: vyg25's construction in GS21
question: Does a priced second factor with heterogeneous firm exposures create a fair complexity gap in GS21, where exposure to the existing state (gx7, bx7) did not?
notes:
THE KP14 CONSTRUCTION ONE MODEL OVER (2026-10-07). vyg25 is the project's only KP14 economy with a fair gap positive in ten seeds of ten (+0.0148), and its mechanism -- a priced stationary state y, three firm types loading cash flows as e^{b_f y}, a y=0 level compensation bv_comp 1.2, price gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35 -- had never been built in BGN or GS21: BGN has no firm type at all (its project-beta continuum is the same distribution for every firm) and GS21's exposure path (gx7, bx7) loaded types on the EXISTING state x, not on a new priced one. This spec adds exactly vyg25's ingredients.

LADDER. gs_bv on the unit-sd y: production exp(x + z + gs_bv y + gs_ashift); KP14's (0.02, 0.07, 0.14) scaled by 0.7. Low-resolution calibration (xnum 41, znum 50, bnum 10, NY 9, 150-firm panel, validate_gs_vy.py, 2026-10-07 22:35 CDT): type premia at gs_bv 0 / 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.2 are 3.2 / 7.6 / 10.5 / 12.9 %/yr (gsbase's is 3.2), the derived gs_ashift 0 / 0.275 / 0.538 / 1.030 and mean log size 4.12 / 4.30 / 4.69 / 5.57: the compensation is a strong LEVEL sort, as KP14's measured footprint is. The ladder (0, 0.05, 0.1) gives SR_max 0.39 / 0.49 / 0.60 by y-tercile, about 0.49 on average -- vyg25's 0.495 and bvy25's 0.49 -- while (0, 0.1, 0.2) gives 0.61 / 0.76 / 0.90 and a 13 %/yr top premium. So the top two exposures are 0.05 and 0.1 and the bottom type gets 0.015 so that, as in KP14, every type loads. NY 9 nodes over +-2.5 sd (spacing 0.625 against s_y 0.238); E[M R] = 1 to 1e-15 on the calibration economies.

CHECKS BEFORE SUBMISSION. gs_solve_vy at NY=1 against gs_solve_reg at gmreg [1,1], low resolution: every table within 7e-12, identical policies (check_parity.py). The smoothing convolution is evaluated in its exact cumulative form (1e-13 against the broadcast form); a full-resolution NY=9 solve runs at ~2 s/sweep, 1.5 GB.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false (new producer, dirty tree); ids are read from the Quest solve logs by fill_gs_vy_ids.py (verify_gs_vy_klc.sh) before any seed runs; this spec was written before the solves.

PREDICTION (2026-10-07, before the run). GS21's exposure path on x (gx7, bx7) made room of +0.008 and no gap; a PRICED new state is the one ingredient those lacked, and the compensation makes the type a level sort of size. Expect room +0.01 to +0.05 with the market still spanning most of SR_max (finding 8), room_s well below room, fair gap between -0.005 and +0.008. FALSIFIED as 'the KP mechanism ports' if the fair gap exceeds +0.010 in 8 of 10 seeds.

changes: new model directory variants/gs_vy (gs_solve_reg's regime replaced by a PRICED NY-node y chain; NY=1 reproduces gsbase)
y: 9-node Tauchen chain over +-2.5 sd of an AR(1) with kappa_y 0.35/yr, priced at gamma_v 2.5
three types in shares [0.34, 0.33, 0.33] with exposures gs_bv [0.015, 0.05, 0.1], bv_comp 1.2 -> gs_ashift derived and applied in solver AND simulator

method.gs_ashift_ladder: derived: -bv_comp log W(gs_bv), applied in solver and simulator

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / bx_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
